about.title: About Us
about.mainText: Mauá Racing is a team composed of students from all degree programs at the Mauá Institute of Technology dedicated to developing and building automotive prototypes for academic competitions. We work on three main projects: Formula Combustion, Formula Hydrogen (H₂), and Baja SAE, each with specific engineering requirements and manufacturing processes. Our work covers the entire vehicle development cycle: from conception, analysis, and simulation to the design of structures, powertrains, suspension systems, brakes, and vehicle dynamics. We also handle manufacturing, assembly, testing, and the final preparation of the prototypes for competition. The team is dedicated to applying theoretical knowledge to practical solutions by integrating engineering methods, management practices, and compliance with technical standards, all while remaining committed to high quality prototypes and the development of competitive vehicles. We participate in competitions organized by SAE Brasil, which establish criteria for performance, efficiency, safety, innovation, and project viability.

aboutFsae.title: About SAE
aboutFsae.firstText: SAE Brasil is a technical association that brings together professionals and students from the fields of engineering and mobility. Among its key activities, it promotes student programs and academic competitions that challenge university teams to design, build, and test vehicles, including Formula-style prototypes and Baja off-road vehicles.
aboutFsae.secondText: Acting as a link between university and industry, SAE Brasil provides a platform for learning, innovation, and technical visibility in the training of future engineers.
aboutFsae.thirdText: Mauá Racing participates in these programs by developing prototypes that meet the performance, safety, and feasibility requirements established by SAE Brasil.
aboutFsae.fourthText: The competition is not only fun and challenging but also an opportunity for growth. The project is carried out in groups to foster and develop teamwork. Furthermore, it offers students the chance to apply theoretical knowledge in a practical setting by developing a complete project. Students also gain visibility among major companies and opportunities for recognition; standout students may even be hired by the major automakers that support the competition.
